character.lede: A sage-yellow farmhouse with a hipped roof, two street gables and a picket-railed wrap veranda stands behind slate-blue shutters and flower boxes. A greenhouse, a gazebo, a pond and rows of garden beds fill the back.

spots.line: A play kitchen, an easel and a toy box fill the playroom.
A glider and a crib stand in the quiet upstairs nursery.
Two rocking chairs and a small table face the garden.

facts.style: Two-storey sage-yellow lap-siding Victorian-farmhouse family home on a raised foundation: hipped roof with two overlapping street gables, a one-storey gabled west wing, a gabled entry portico and a picket-railed wrap veranda, slate-blue louvred shutters and flower boxes on every window, a warm cream wainscoted living room with a canted garden bay, and a backyard homestead (lily pond with a gazebo on a boardwalk, glass greenhouse, staggered raised beds, monkey bars)

character.truths: The Core sits on a console table in the Living Room, in sight of the door. There is no television. The kitchen has a breakfast bar. A crib stands in the Living Room as well as the Nursery. Greenhouse, gazebo, pond, garden beds and monkey bars.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
nextcloud: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Nextcloud as a recommended app.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
yuvomi: [note] Stored in SQLite on your Core. CalDAV and CardDAV sync are optional.
one household planner, not an account per person
already in the persona pool: share cap risk
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
bentopdf: Dual licence: AGPL-3.0 or paid commercial; fine for household use
Listing says "nothing to leak": drop that wording
tandoor: [note] Overlaps Mealie; pick one per story.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
vaultwarden: [note] Bitwarden-compatible server, unofficial. Do not say "Bitwarden".
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
libreoffice: [note] The listing is generic. Name the suite, not specific features.
[note] ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors does the same job: one suite per household.
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
kiwix: marketplace: Ships with an empty library: the compose runs kiwix-serve on /data/library.xml with no content and no way in the Hub to add or register ZIM files; the QA capture shows "No result".
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
excalidraw: [note] amd64 only. An Excalidraw MCP entry exists for agents.
marketplace: Manifest source points to ozencb/excalidraw-persist, a 105-star wrapper, not excalidraw/excalidraw.
habitica: The sign-up page in the capture carries a cookie-consent banner: check the self-hosted build for analytics scripts before saying it sends nothing out
Game, not a health or behaviour tool: no outcomes
kokoro: [note] OpenAI-compatible speech API. No GPU requirement in the listing.
OpenAI-compatible speech API; web player included.
No GPU requirement in the listing; no speed claim.
Capture is real (FastKoko player) on a dark purple background.
donetick: [cloud-link] Notifications use Telegram or Pushover. Both are outside services.
NFC-tag completion needs a phone that reads NFC on the home network
homebox: [note] Barcode and Open Food Facts lookups call outside services.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Analytics are switched off in the manifest (good)
pingvin-share: [public-access] Recipients outside your home network need to reach your Core.
public-access for anyone outside the house
miniflux: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Integrations push to outside services if switched on (Pocket, Telegram, webhooks)
twenty: marketplace: QA capture shows real company names and logos.
solidtime: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
listing mentions invoices: say nothing about billing or tax
